old: This word for a sudden catastrophe was once a literal verdict handed down by the position of the sky.
Its two Italian building blocks mean “bad” and “star” — misfortune was once blamed directly on an unlucky alignment overhead.
The “star” half also shows up in astronomy and astronaut; the “bad” half resurfaces in disgrace and discord.
clues: This noun for a sudden turn of events was once a literal astrological verdict, blaming misfortune on an unfavorable alignment of the stars.
Today it means a sudden event causing great damage or loss, like a flood or earthquake, or jokingly a total flop. It is the everyday word, commoner than catastrophe.
Relief agencies respond to the natural kind, and a risky plan is called a recipe for one. Its star root reappears in astronomy and astronaut.
